sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Luther Hon, Adedamola Aregbesola, Thelma Araokanmi, John Muniru & David Onoja. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Some Endangered West Chadic A.2 Bole Languages of Bauchi State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-011 (92 pp.). Dallas: SIL International. (SIL archive entry 94412)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only work with any Daza language data (222-item wordlist, Kadoli, Luther Hon, 2 May 2021, Appendix F). Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventory' (pp. 32-34) gives pooled consonant/vowel charts for six Bole languages as 'initial, cursory observations' from wordlists only; Appendix F p. 55: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Wordlist is tone-marked phonetic transcription (e.g. 'hair' [sókíː]); no word on stress/accent or on the tone system. p. 6: the only earlier mentions of Daza are Temple (1922) and S…

sources.note: Family-level only ('All Chadic languages are tone languages'); nothing specific to Daza, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1978. Introduction. In Bole-Tangale Languages of the Bauchi Area (Northern Nigeria) (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A 13), 1-16. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Daza data at all: p. 10 'Daza has never been reported in the literature to my knowledge. Its existence was reported by Kirfi and Bele speakers.. it is fairly certain that such a language exists'. The group-level remark p. 9 ('These languages all have two phonemic tones only') rests on the eight languages he recorded, not Daza. No mention of stress/accent anywhere in the book.

sources.citation: SIL Nigeria language survey team (Yakubu Danladi, Luther Hon et al.). 2021. Daza (Kadoli) survey field recordings and wordlist audio, February/May 2021. Unpublished; SIL Nigeria, Jos (possibly to be deposited in SIL Language & Culture Archives / REAP).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The audio behind the Appendix F wordlist is the only material from which prominence/tone in Daza could ever be described; no analysis has been published.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2018-. West Chadic A.2 (Bole group) comparative wordlists, Bauchi State (unpublished; 'nothing is published yet' per Decker et al. 2022 p. 6).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: If Blench/Bulkaam ever recorded Daza (Decker lists them only for Gera), their tone-marked lists sometimes carry brief phonology notes; would be the only other conceivable source.
